-2nCxItGNvE.label: GTC 2026
-2nCxItGNvE.description:
A silent revolution in AI is rewriting the rules of computation. Autonomous, self-evolving ""claws"" like OpenClaw are now being adopted at an unprecedented pace, demonstrating their ability to execute complex, long-running goals indefinitely. These agents write code, manage entire workflows, and access local files, ushering in the new application layer for AI. But with unprecedented self-evolving capability, guardrails are essential to give users control over how agents behave and handle data. Watch to understand this explosive shift and the infrastructure emerging to govern long-running agents more safely.

Learn more about how to run autonomous agents safely: https://www.nvidia.com/nemoclaw

#OpenClaw #NVIDIAGTC #AgenticAI

7N38fD4ksnI.label: GTC 2026
7N38fD4ksnI.description: Autonomous vehicles (AVs) are emerging as the first mass-deployed physical AI agents, reshaping mobility and driving new demands in AI, safety, and scalable development. This special address explores the industry’s path to Level 4 autonomy and how NVIDIA is helping accelerate it. With the DRIVE Hyperion architecture, manufacturers (OEMs) and AV developers can build scalable, safety-certified autonomy solutions. NVIDIA will present its cloud-to-car platform—spanning training, simulation, and in-vehicle compute—to support developing and validating next-generation drive-policy models. The session will also touch on how agentic AI is poised to transform AVs end to end, from automating data-driven development and validation to enabling more intelligent, adaptive in-car experiences. Gain insights into L4 software architectures, the DRIVE Hyperion platform, and ecosystem collaboration across OEMs, AV developers, mobility providers, and robotaxi companies.

BAhI87RS-DQ.description:
AI literacy has moved from a "nice-to-have" to a readiness requirement. The open question is execution: how schools build access that scales, supports educators, and reaches students across different learning paths, geographies, and resources.

This panel brings together education leaders and practitioners shaping that execution from four angles: classroom and school implementation, learning science and workforce-relevant skill-building, platform-level delivery at scale, and institutional systems that connect education to long-term opportunity.

Together, the panel will share practical approaches to expand AI literacy and access without turning schools into pilot sites. You'll leave with a clear view of what to teach, how to equip educators, how to deploy tools responsibly, and how to build pathways that connect early literacy to real-world readiness over time.

We can’t wait to see what you do next.
